standard_prerequisites.name: Multiplicative structure of alpha^{omega(n)}
standard_prerequisites.statement: alpha^{omega(n)} is multiplicative, so the Dirichlet series-type sums over n with all prime factors bounded factor as Euler products.
standard_prerequisites.use: The case y >= sqrt(x) writes the sum as a product over primes p <= y^3 at source line 1691.

standard_prerequisites.name: Strong Mertens estimate
standard_prerequisites.statement: sum over prime powers p^k <= x of 1/(k p^k) = log log x + gamma + O(1/(log x)^3).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used at source line 1693 to control the Euler product.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dyadic summation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A sum over an interval may be split into dyadic blocks (e^{m-1}, e^m] and bounded by the number of blocks times the largest block.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the technique of the case y <= sqrt(x) at source lines 1695-1699.

core_obligations: Derive the first bound from the cited classical estimate (source line 1687).

For the second bound in the range y >= sqrt(x), enlarge the range to all n whose prime factors are at most y^3, factor the sum as an Euler product, and bound it by (log y)^alpha using 1+t <= e^t and Mertens's estimate (source lines 1689-1693).
For the range y <= sqrt(x), split the interval [x/y, xy] into dyadic blocks (e^{m-1}, e^m] and bound each block by e^{1-m} times the sum of alpha^{omega(n)} up to e^m (source lines 1695-1698).
Apply the first part of the proposition to each block to get the factor e^m (log(xy))^{alpha-1}, and count the blocks to obtain the extra factor log y (source line 1699).

proof_roadmap.step: First bound by the cited estimate.
Large-y case by an Euler product and Mertens's estimate.
Dyadic decomposition in the small-y case.
Apply the first bound blockwise and count the blocks.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prel:partial summation bounds` at source lines 1678-1685: two uniform bounds, sum over n <= x of alpha^{omega(n)} << x (log x)^{alpha-1} and sum over x/y < n <= xy of alpha^{omega(n)}/n << (log y)(log(xy))^{alpha-1}, for alpha in [0,1] and x, y >= 2. The author's proof (source lines 1687-1700) splits into two genuinely different regimes: when y >= sqrt(x) the second sum is enlarged to a sum over numbers with all prime factors at most y^3, factored as an Euler product and bounded with 1+t <= e^t along with the strong Mertens estimate (lines 1689-1693); when y <= sqrt(x) the interval is decomposed into dyadic blocks and each block is controlled by the first bound of the proposition, with the count of blocks producing the factor log y (lines 1695-1699). The statement is two inequalities and records neither the Euler product nor the dyadic splitting.
